title: Control Moment Gyroscopes
description: Control moment gyroscopes are spinning flywheels on gimbals that produce large righting torques when tilted. Unlike a passive gyro, a CMG steers its spin axis to push back against any roll, holding the pod upright even at a standstill. In practical terms: A 20-kilogram flywheel at 10,000 RPM stores serious angular momentum; Gimbal rates of a few radians per second generate car-scale righting torque; and Counter-rotating pairs cancel unwanted yaw reactions.

Gimbal rates of a few radians per second generate car-scale righting torque.
Counter-rotating pairs cancel unwanted yaw reactions.
